frontier.hypothesis: The one unexplored deletion surface in the whole grind: an insn counted by flow AND by sched1, present through global_alloc, and deleted AFTER it (reload's no-op-move deletion, jump2 cross-jumping) is simultaneously a counted reference and byte-free -- exactly the shape out2's missing fourth reference needs.
frontier.mechanism: global_alloc reads reg_n_refs and reg_live_length before reload / sched2 / jump2 / reorg run, so every closure in this ledger (which stops at combine and local-alloc) leaves this surface untested -- E-s29-3 named it and no session probed it. reload deletes a (set p1 p2) that becomes a no-op once both pseudos land on the same hard register; the block-2 `out3 = out2;` copy is already a counted reference to out2 and would be byte-free if out3 were seated on out2's own $s6.
frontier.next_probe: On the S1 chassis, force out3 off $s3 (which is free in loop2 only because stptr is dead there) by giving loop2 a live carrier that outranks out3, and check with `bash tmp/grind/func_80041188/s33/fr.sh <TAG> 87 86` whether pseudo 87 lands on $s6, whether the `move` disappears from the sandbox object, and what the insn count does. The question this answers is project-wide: can a copy be both flow-counted and unemitted in GCC 2.7.2?

frontier.hypothesis: The block-2 copy can be made combine-deletable (E-s28-2 shape A) by giving out3 a SINGLE use, so flow still counts out2's fourth reference while the move folds into an argument setup target already emits.
frontier.mechanism: Shape A deletes a reg-reg copy whose destination has one use (verified on insns 4 and 43 of the V15a dump). out3 has three references today (def + two loop2 uses), which is the only reason the copy survives to emission as `move $s3,$s6`. Loop2's two consumers are both argument moves, so a second carrier may fold into moves target already has.
frontier.next_probe: Spell loop2 with out3 read once and a second local taking the other use (both orders), measure sandbox and the ALLOCDBG references for pseudos 86/87 and the new pseudo; watch for the two carriers conflicting and materialising a real move (+1 insn, the s21-era in-loop detour failure mode). Bank either way -- this is the last untried spelling of E-s29-1's conservation law.

frontier.hypothesis: The fifth parameter may be a struct whose first two members are the matrix pair followed by fields loop2 or block 2 touches; if so, a natural member access could read &m[1] and deliver out2's fourth reference as ordinary C rather than as a construct.
frontier.mechanism: E-s33-3's semantic closure of block 2 assumes the parameter is exactly a two-element matrix pair. func_8004A348 / func_800523E0 / func_80044DE4 are INCLUDE_ASM with exactly one caller (this function, E-s32-4), so the type has to come from their bodies rather than from a matched sibling.
frontier.next_probe: Read asm/funcs/func_8004A348.s, func_800523E0.s and func_80044DE4.s far enough to see which offsets of their matrix arguments are loaded/stored and whether anything touches past +0x40 of the pair. If something does, re-spell block 2's out3 definition as a member access and measure; if nothing does, record the pair type as confirmed and close this frontier, leaving FRONTIER 1 as the last open surface.
